lesson.title: Technology of the Industrial Age
lesson.summary: How steam engines, railroads, steamships, the telegraph, and later steel and electricity transformed production, transport, and communication.
learningGoals: Explain how technology shaped economic production over time.
Distinguish the first industrial technologies from the second wave after 1850.
lesson.bigIdea: New energy sources and machines transformed how goods were made and moved and how information traveled.
lesson.context: The steam engine was the key early technology. Later, steel, electricity, and chemistry produced a second wave of industrial change.

sections.title: Steam and transport

blocks.text: James Watt's improvements to the steam engine made it far more efficient. Steam powered factories, then locomotives and ships. The Liverpool and Manchester Railway opened in 1830.
Railroads and steamships lowered transport costs and tied distant regions into national and global markets. The telegraph sent messages almost instantly; a transatlantic cable worked from 1866.

blocks.title: Cause and effect
blocks.text: Cheaper and faster transport and communication expanded markets, which encouraged larger factories and more specialized production.

sections.takeaway: Steam and electricity shrank distances for goods and information.

sections.title: A second wave

blocks.text: After 1850, the Bessemer process made steel cheap. Electricity, chemicals, and the internal combustion engine created new industries.
Germany and the United States led many of these industries, investing in research laboratories and engineers.

sections.takeaway: Science-based industries made Germany and the United States industrial leaders.

connections.title: From sail to steam
connections.body: Unit 4 described ships that depended on winds and currents. Steamships freed ocean travel from the wind.
connections.transferQuestion: How did steamships change ocean travel compared with sailing ships?
connections.feedback: Compare dependence on wind and the speed or reliability of voyages.
